region: Western Hajar Mountains, Jebel Akhdar and Ad Dhahirah
title: Oman — The Hajar Beyond the Circuit
subtitle: The Oman you haven't seen: canyon rims, abandoned mountain villages and Bronze Age tombs, with the classic coast-and-desert loop left out.
summary: A 12-day inland route through the Western Hajar: Wadi Bani Awf and Snake Gorge, tent nights on the Jebel Shams rim, the Bat–Al-Ayn tombs near Ibri and the Jebel Akhdar terraces. It deliberately avoids Musandam, Salalah, Duqm and the Yemen border, which French or Dutch advice marks orange.
introduction: Most visitors see Oman as a loop from Muscat to Nizwa, the Wahiba Sands and Sur. This trip stays in the mountains and the inland plain instead. It starts with the Wadi Bani Awf track and a guided descent of Snake Gorge, then spends two tent nights on the Jebel Shams canyon rim and walks the cliff-edge Balcony Walk to the abandoned village of Sab Bani Khamis. A drive west reaches the beehive tombs of Bat and Al-Ayn near Ibri, followed by the Jebel Akhdar terraces and the empty gorge village of Wadi Bani Habib. Dhofar, Duqm and Musandam are left out because French advice lists them as orange.

exceptional.vsOman: This is Oman itself, so the comparison is with the classic circuit of Muscat, Nizwa, Wahiba Sands and Sur. This plan skips the sands, the Sharqiya coast and the turtle beaches and spends ten nights in the Western Hajar and Ad Dhahirah, mostly at 1,000–2,000 m with cold nights. The southern and northern 'other Oman' (Dhofar, Duqm, Musandam) is not offered, because France lists Salalah, Duqm and Musandam as orange and the Netherlands lists Musandam as orange.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Package Oman runs Muscat, Wahiba camps and Wadi Shab by coach, with Jebel Shams as a lookout stop. Here the group descends a canyon with a local guide, walks the cliff edge with no guardrails, camps on the rim, and sleeps in village guesthouses rather than resorts.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: The portfolio's other mountain routes lack the combination of a 1,000 m canyon rim you can camp on, a Bronze Age UNESCO necropolis and terraced mountain villages on one self-drive loop of about 1,300 km.

duration.note: Day 1 is the evening departure from Paris and day 12 the return flight; with an overnight arrival, the first full day starts in Muscat on day 2.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: Ramadan is expected to run from about 8 February to 9 March 2027, with Eid al-Fitr on 9 or 10 March. Leaving on 13 March starts the trip after Eid, with daytime eating and normal opening hours restored, while Jebel Shams and Jebel Akhdar are still cool (Saiq mean 17 °C by day and 9.5 °C by night in March). Heat starts to build on the Ibri plain (mean 32.5 °C by day).

februarySuitability.summary: Cool, dry-weather conditions suit trekking, but Ramadan covers roughly 8 February onwards: only 1–7 February are free of it. Eating and drinking in public in daylight is a punishable offence, even for non-Muslims, and many village cafés close by day.

marchSuitability.summary: After Eid, mountain days are 15–22 °C and nights 3–10 °C on the rims, which suits camping with proper sleeping bags and long walks. Showers can still cause flash floods in wadis, and Eid weekends can fill the guesthouses.

climate.regionNote: Figures combine three NOAA/WMO-based stations given on Wikipedia: Muscat (coast), Saiq (Jebel Akhdar plateau, about 1,950 m) and Ibri (Ad Dhahirah plain). Jebel Shams rim temperatures (about 2,000 m) are not published in the sources and are estimated as similar to or a few degrees below Saiq.

february.rainfall: Muscat about 6.5 mm in the month; Saiq about 60 mm, the wettest period of the year on the plateau, with thunderstorms possible.
february.notes: Muscat 26/18 °C, Saiq 13.5/6.4 °C, Ibri 29/15 °C (mean max/min). Rim nights near freezing are possible; the minimum of 3 °C is an estimate.

march.rainfall: Muscat about 11.5 mm; Saiq about 52 mm; showers on the mountains can flood wadis within hours.
march.notes: Muscat 29/20 °C, Saiq 17/9.5 °C, Ibri 32.5/18.6 °C (mean max/min). Take a three-season sleeping bag for the rims.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: Snow is not expected on the route; Saiq has recorded below-freezing nights in the past. Mountain access depends on rain: the Wadi Bani Awf track and the Jebel Shams road are unpaved in parts and can close after storms. The Jebel Akhdar road is tarmac but has a police checkpoint that admits 4x4 vehicles only.
climate.seaConditions: Not relevant: the route is inland. The Gulf of Oman is not part of the plan because of maritime-attack and piracy advisories.
climate.airQuality: Generally good in the mountains; dust haze possible on the Ibri plain.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Not a wildlife trip. Goats and camels on roads are a hazard.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Ramadan
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Eating, drinking and smoking in public in daylight is illegal. Trip is timed to start after it ends.

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Eid al-Fitr
holidaysAndFestivals.dates: ≈ 9–10 Mar 2027, public holiday of several days
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Omani families travel to Jebel Akhdar and Jebel Shams; guesthouses fill and fares to Muscat peak. The trip starts on 13 March, at the tail end of the holiday.

climate.ramadan2027: Expected to begin about 8 February 2027 and end with Eid al-Fitr on 9 or 10 March (moon sighting; no Omani official date yet). During Ramadan, eating, drinking and smoking in public in daylight is punishable, shops and cafés close by day, forts keep short hours and guides fast, which makes long exposed walks harder. The route is therefore planned for 13–24 March, after the holiday.
climate.lunarNewYear2027: Not relevant: Lunar New Year (6 February 2027) has no effect on this route.
climate.tourismDemand: March is the end of the cool season, but the Hajar is lightly visited by foreigners compared with Muscat and Wahiba. Eid weekends and Fridays bring Omani and Gulf families to Jebel Akhdar and Jebel Shams.
climate.flightPriceSeasonality: Fares usually rise around Eid and fall afterwards, but French spring-holiday demand only starts in April. Easter is on 28 March 2027. Fares in 2026 were also shaped by regional-conflict disruption; no live fare was seen.

geography.summary: The Western Hajar is a limestone and ophiolite range rising to about 3,000 m, cut by deep wadis and terraced plateaus. On the west side, the Ad Dhahirah plain opens into gravel desert.
geography.distinctive: Jebel Shams, the highest part of the Hajar, has a canyon rim about 1,000 m deep that visitors can camp beside, and Jebel Akhdar has irrigated terraces at about 2,000 m. Both are reached on roads that tourists on the classic circuit rarely take.

landscapes.name: Jebel Shams canyon (Wadi Nakhr)
landscapes.description: A canyon with walls about 1,000 m high at the plateau rim, with the Balcony Walk along the side.

landscapes.name: Wadi Bani Awf and Snake Gorge
landscapes.description: A mountain track and slot-and-boulder gorge with pools, linking the Batinah side to Balad Sayt and Al Hamra.

landscapes.name: Jebel Akhdar terraces
landscapes.description: Stepped gardens of walnuts, apricots and pomegranates fed by stone channels at about 2,000 m.

landscapes.name: Ad Dhahirah plain and Jebel Misht
landscapes.description: Gravel plain at the foot of the Hajar's western edge, with the Bronze Age tomb ridges beneath Jebel Misht.

culture.summary: Two layers: a third-millennium BC tomb landscape near Ibri, and mountain villages with irrigation channels, abandoned stone settlements and 17th–18th century forts that show how Hajar communities lived before roads.

culturalHighlights.name: Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn
culturalHighlights.description: Necropolis of beehive tombs and a tower dating to the third millennium BC (Hafit period), inscribed on the World Heritage List in 1988. Quiet and open, with the tombs at Al-Ayn on a ridge below Jebel Misht.

culturalHighlights.name: Misfat Al Abriyyin
culturalHighlights.description: Stone and mud-brick houses with irrigated palm and banana terraces; the walk on the lanes and beside the water channels shows the falaj irrigation system that sustains Hajar villages. Staying in a family-run guesthouse supports local income.

culturalHighlights.name: Wadi Bani Habib and Al Aqor
culturalHighlights.description: An abandoned village at the bottom of a gorge with terraced orchards that are still worked, and Al Aqor, a village reached only on foot. Visit with a local guide and keep to the paths.

culturalHighlights.name: Nakhal Fort and Al Hazm Castle
culturalHighlights.description: Forts of the Imamate period near Rustaq and Nakhal, the stop between plateau and coast.

adventureHighlights.name: Snake Gorge descent
adventureHighlights.description: Guided canyon descent of 3–6 hours with swims, jumps into pools and, on the upper route, abseils. The lower canyon is listed with no mandatory abseil. Cold water in March.

adventureHighlights.name: Balcony Walk (W6) to Sab Bani Khamis
adventureHighlights.description: About 7–8 km return, 3–4 hours on a cliff-edge path with no guardrails; easy underfoot, exposed for anyone uneasy with heights.

adventureHighlights.name: Wadi Bani Awf mountain crossing
adventureHighlights.description: Self-drive on a steep, partly unpaved track with narrow ledges, from the Batinah side to Balad Sayt; a 4x4 is strongly recommended and the track must be skipped after rain.

adventureHighlights.name: Jebel Akhdar walks
adventureHighlights.description: Wadi Bani Habib and the Al Aqor–Sayq path (W18b) on terraces and steps at about 2,000 m, best with a local guide.

signatureExperiences.title: Snake Gorge descent in Wadi Bani Awf
signatureExperiences.description: Walk, swim and slide through the lower Snake Canyon with a licensed local guide, then return to Balad Sayt for the night.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: One of Oman's few guided canyon descents, in the same wadi the group has just driven through, with village overnight stays at both ends.
signatureExperiences.location: Wadi Bani Awf, Wilayat of Rustaq
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book a day trip or private guide in advance with a local operator; tiers listed for the lower canyon are 70 OMR for one person, 35 OMR each for 2–4 and 30 OMR each for 5–8 (operator programme page). Confirm the pick-up point, wetsuits and the water level the evening before.
signatureExperiences.costNote: 35 OMR at about 2.2 EUR per OMR is about 77 EUR; 85 EUR includes VAT and transfer allowance. Estimate; quotes not obtained.

signatureExperiences.title: Two nights on the Jebel Shams rim and the Balcony Walk
signatureExperiences.description: Camp near the canyon rim, walk the W6 Balcony Walk on the next morning and watch the light change on the wall of Wadi Nakhr.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A canyon about 1,000 m deep that you sleep beside, and an abandoned cliff village at the end of the walk.
signatureExperiences.location: Jebel Shams, Wilayat of Al Hamra
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Drive from Al Hamra on the paved road that becomes gravel near the rim; a 4x4 is recommended. Use an established campsite or guesthouse near the rim, bring cold-rated sleeping bags and carry water; the trail has no facilities.
signatureExperiences.costNote: The walk is free; camping fees are in the budget under campsite fees.

signatureExperiences.title: Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn at sunset
signatureExperiences.description: Visit the UNESCO beehive tombs near Ibri, with the Al-Ayn ridge in late-afternoon light.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A Bronze Age necropolis on open ground near Ibri, far from the usual circuit and visited by few foreigners.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Self-drive from Ibri; sites are reached by road. Plan the Al-Ayn tombs for late afternoon, confirm access and hours locally and bring insect repellent.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Fees and hours not verified; none expected.

signatureExperiences.title: Jebel Akhdar terraces and Wadi Bani Habib
signatureExperiences.description: A day of guided walking among stepped gardens, irrigation channels and the abandoned village in Wadi Bani Habib, with an optional section of the Al Aqor–Sayq path.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Terrace farming at about 2,000 m and a ruined village at the bottom of a gorge, in a landscape still worked by villagers.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Self-drive on the tarmac road from Birkat Al Mawz (police checkpoint, 4x4 only) and hire a local guide for the day; guide cost shared by the group.
signatureExperiences.costNote: One guide-day of about 70 EUR shared by four. Estimate.

signatureExperiences.title: Driving the Wadi Bani Awf track
signatureExperiences.description: Self-drive the mountain crossing from the Batinah side to Balad Sayt and Al Hamra in a 4x4, with Little Snake Canyon and Balad Sayt on the way.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A mountain road with steep sections and ledges, linking two governorates through the heart of the Western Hajar.
signatureExperiences.location: Wadi Bani Awf, Rustaq to Al Hamra
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Start early in dry weather; carry water, tell a third party your route; avoid it during or after rain. A private driver is an option for those not comfortable with narrow ledges.

travelStyle.summary: One shared 4x4 driven by the two licensed drivers on short mountain stages of 2–4.5 hours, with tent nights on the Jebel Shams rim and village guesthouses elsewhere, and two guided days.

transport.summary: A single rented 4x4 for ten days; no domestic flights. Guided days are arranged locally.

modes.description: Needed for the Wadi Bani Awf track, the Jebel Shams road and the Jebel Akhdar checkpoint; seats four adults with camping gear.
The Snake Gorge descent and the Wadi Bani Habib walk use the operator's guide and, where offered, its pick-up.
A driver-guide for the Wadi Bani Awf crossing is possible for those who prefer not to drive narrow ledges.

transport.carRental: 4x4 daily rates seen in Muscat range from 42 OMR for a Fortuner-class vehicle at one local agency (38 OMR for 11+ days, optional CDW at 6 OMR/day, CDW excess 300 OMR) to USD 143 per day for a 2026 Prado listing; the Prado is the benchmark. Drivers must be 21–75 with at least 1 year of licence at the agency read. Airport surcharges and one-way fees are not confirmed; the trip is round-trip from Muscat so none applies. Confirm in writing that the contract covers off-road tracks, the Wadi Bani Awf crossing and the Jebel Akhdar road, and lists a second driver.

drivingRequirements.summary: Roads are mostly good. The Wadi Bani Awf track is unpaved in parts, with narrow ledges; the Jebel Shams road is paved then gravel near the rim; Jebel Akhdar is tarmac but only 4x4 vehicles pass the checkpoint. Traffic enforcement is strict, with fines up to 3,000 OMR or prison, and wandering camels and goats are a hazard.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: Not verified for French licences. The UK FCDO says a UK photocard licence can be used for the first six weeks, and rental companies often have stricter requirements, including holding an IDP. Check the rental contract and carry an IDP if the company asks for one.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four hold car licences and drive in turn, with both registered as drivers on the contract. Plan 2–4.5 hours of driving a day and no night driving in the mountains.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: Nobody should ride a motorcycle or quad without the legally required licence; no riding is planned. Legal alternatives: guided 4x4 days, a driver-guide for mountain stages, or walking.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: One 4x4 with two drivers, a satellite messenger or phone, and a third party who knows the route. France advises convoys of at least two vehicles for desert excursions; this route is mountain and village driving, but the same logic applies to the Wadi Bani Awf crossing, which should be driven early in dry weather.

accommodation.summary: Village guesthouses and simple hotels, with three tent nights on the Jebel Shams rim and near Balad Sayt.
types: Village guesthouse (Balad Sayt, Misfat Al Abriyyin)
Small hotel in Ibri and Rustaq
Guesthouse or small hotel on Jebel Akhdar

camping.summary: Wild camping is a popular pastime in Oman, away from private land and livestock; campers should pitch on high ground and keep out of wadi beds because of flash floods, which have caused deaths. Muscat Governorate requires a municipality licence (reported rules from 2022), nature reserves require permits, so the route avoids camping near Muscat. Nights on the rims are cold (3–10 °C).

physicalDifficulty.label: demanding
physicalDifficulty.summary: Walking days of 3–6 hours at about 2,000 m, a cold-water canyon descent and cliff-edge paths. No technical climbing, but the group needs hiking fitness, comfort with heights and swimming ability.

itinerary.summary: Twelve days from Paris: a drive from Muscat into the Wadi Bani Awf track, a guided canyon day, two tent nights on the Jebel Shams rim, west to the Bat–Al-Ayn tombs near Ibri, three days on Jebel Akhdar and its terraces, then back to Muscat via Nakhal and Rustaq. Day 10 is a contingency day.

days.title: Evening departure from Paris
activities: Fly Paris CDG to Muscat; with a nonstop operated by Oman Air (about 7 hours) the flight is overnight, otherwise one stop via a Gulf or Turkish hub
Check that passports are valid for at least six months after the planned exit date
days.travelTime: ≈ 7 h nonstop if flying; 9–12 h with one stop
days.practical: Nonstop schedule not verified for 2027. Carry proof of onward travel, accommodation for the first night and travel health insurance for immigration.

days.title: Muscat to the Wadi Bani Awf track
activities: Arrive in the early morning if flying the overnight nonstop; clear immigration (free visa stamp for up to 14 days) and collect the 4x4
Buy water, food and a local SIM in Seeb or Barka
Drive to Rustaq and enter Wadi Bani Awf on the track to Balad Sayt, stopping at viewpoints and Little Snake Canyon
Settle in at a Balad Sayt guesthouse
days.transport: Rental 4x4 (shared by the two licensed drivers)
days.travelTime: ≈ 4.5–5 h driving including the slow track
days.practical: Long day after a night flight; if arrival is on a later flight, sleep in Seeb and start on day 3. Drive the track in daylight and only in dry weather.

days.title: Snake Gorge with a local guide
activities: Meet the guide at Balad Sayt and descend the lower Snake Canyon: walking, swimming and sliding, 3–6 hours
Return to the village, rest and explore the palm gardens
Camp or stay a second night at Balad Sayt
days.travelTime: ≈ 1 h by vehicle plus 3–6 h on foot
days.accommodation: Tent or guesthouse in Balad Sayt (tent night 1)
days.practical: If the water is high or rain is forecast the guide may refuse the descent: the fallback is Little Snake Canyon on foot or a rest day. Wetsuit hire and cold water in March.

days.title: Balad Sayt to Al Hamra and the Jebel Shams rim
activities: Drive the mountain track to Al Hamra
Walk the lanes and falaj channels of Misfat Al Abriyyin and eat lunch in the village
Drive the paved then gravel road to the canyon rim; set up the tents before sunset
days.travelTime: ≈ 2.5–3 h to Al Hamra, 1 h to the rim; 4 h with the village stop
days.accommodation: Tent on the Jebel Shams rim (tent night 2)
days.culturalHighlight: Misfat Al Abriyyin and its irrigation channels
days.geographicalHighlight: Wadi Nakhr canyon rim at about 2,000 m
days.practical: Carry two days of water. Nights drop to about 3–10 °C; put the tents up before dark.

days.title: Balcony Walk to Sab Bani Khamis
activities: Walk the W6 Balcony Walk along the canyon wall to the abandoned village of Sab Bani Khamis: about 7–8 km return, 3–4 hours
Rest in the shade; rim viewpoints at sunset
Second night on the rim
days.transport: On foot; 4x4 to and from the trailhead
days.accommodation: Tent on the Jebel Shams rim (tent night 3)
days.culturalHighlight: Abandoned terrace village of Sab Bani Khamis
days.geographicalHighlight: 1,000 m canyon wall with no guardrails
days.practical: Start early; the return is hot. Do not walk if rain is forecast or anyone is uneasy with heights; there are no facilities on the trail.

days.title: West to Ibri and the Al-Ayn tombs
activities: Drive down to Al Hamra and west on the main road to Ibri
Late-afternoon visit to the Al-Ayn beehive tombs beneath Jebel Misht
Check in at an Ibri hotel and eat in town
days.geographicalHighlight: Edge of the Ad Dhahirah plain
days.practical: Time the tomb visit for late afternoon; insects can be a nuisance. Allow for the drive back to Ibri in daylight.

days.title: Bat and Al-Khutm, then up to Jebel Akhdar
activities: Visit Bat and the Al-Khutm tower in the morning
Drive east through Bahla and Nizwa to Birkat Al Mawz without stopping long
Climb the tarmac road to the plateau through the police checkpoint (4x4 only) and check in at a guesthouse or small hotel at Saiq
days.accommodation: Guesthouse or small hotel on the Jebel Akhdar plateau
days.practical: Friday: observe prayer times and expect short opening hours. Brake with a low gear on the descent, not the foot brake.

days.title: Wadi Bani Habib and the terraces
activities: Walk with a local guide to the abandoned village of Wadi Bani Habib, with orchards still worked beside it
Optionally walk a section of the Al Aqor–Sayq path through terrace villages
Evening on the plateau
days.accommodation: Guesthouse or small hotel on the Jebel Akhdar plateau
days.practical: Guide required in practice for the longer path; keep to the steps and tracks and do not enter ruins that look unstable.

days.title: Down to Nakhal and Rustaq
activities: Descend through the checkpoint to Birkat Al Mawz
Drive north to Nakhal for the fort and, if time allows, the Ain Thowarah hot spring
Continue to Rustaq and visit the fort; Al Hazm Castle if time remains
days.accommodation: Small hotel or guesthouse in Rustaq
days.practical: Fort hours and fees to be confirmed locally.

days.title: Contingency and slow day
activities: Use for a washed-out canyon or rim day, a rest day, Al Hazm Castle or a short walk near Rustaq
Prepare gear for the return
days.accommodation: Small hotel or guesthouse in Rustaq
days.practical: Flexible day. Floods or a closed track on days 2–5 would be absorbed here.

days.title: Return to Muscat
activities: Drive back to Seeb, fill the tank and return the 4x4
Free afternoon in Muscat or Seeb; hotel near the airport
days.practical: Return the car with a full tank; check for damage claims and traffic fines, which must be paid before leaving Oman.

days.title: Flight home
activities: Airport check-in; flight to Paris
days.travelTime: ≈ 7 h nonstop; 9–12 h with one stop
days.practical: If the Wednesday nonstop is not operating, book a one-stop alternative and plan for arrival the same day or the next morning.

security.summary: Conditional. The redesigned route stays out of every area that France, the Netherlands or Germany list as orange or warned against (Musandam, Salalah, Duqm, Yemen border), and the UK has no warning for Oman. But official advice conflicts: Canada says avoid non-essential travel, the US and Australia say reconsider travel (as summarised, not read), the UK says the risk of sudden regional escalation is high, and missile and drone attacks have struck targets in Oman in 2026. Flight cancellations, airspace closures and insurance exclusions are material uncertainties.
security.assessedRoute: Muscat (Seeb) – Wadi Bani Awf and Balad Sayt (Al Batinah South) – Al Hamra, Misfat Al Abriyyin and Jebel Shams – Ibri, Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn (Ad Dhahirah) – Birkat Al Mawz and Jebel Akhdar – Nakhal – Rustaq – Seeb. Not in the route: Musandam, Dhofar/Salalah, Duqm and Al Wusta, the Yemen border, Sohar port and industrial areas, the Strait of Hormuz coast, the sea.

conflictRisk.note: Regional conflict since early 2026 involving Iran; the UK describes the risk of sudden escalation as high and Canada reports missile and drone attacks that struck targets in Oman. The route is inland and far from Musandam and Hormuz, but airspace and flights remain exposed.

terrorismRisk.note: FCDO says attacks cannot be ruled out, citing the July 2024 shooting near a mosque in the Wadi Kabir area of Muscat. The Netherlands sees no acute threat. France notes risk of infiltration from Yemen in Dhofar, which the route avoids.

kidnappingRisk.note: No kidnapping warning found in the advisories read; US sources report detentions at the Yemen border, which the route avoids.

regionalRestrictions: Avoid Musandam, the Salalah and Duqm regions and the Yemen border area (France; Musandam and Yemen border per the Netherlands, Germany).
Stay clear of military sites, critical infrastructure and oil and gas facilities; photographing them can lead to severe penalties.
Drones require a licence; unlicensed use can mean a year in prison and a 10,000 OMR fine (France).
Rental vehicles are no longer permitted to enter Musandam from the UAE (France), which matters if the group tried to add it.
ordinaryRisks: Flash floods in wadis: several deaths in 2024; never enter or camp in a wadi when rain is forecast and for at least a day afterwards (FCDO).
Road traffic: accident rates are high; camels and goats on roads; steep mountain tracks and brake fade.
Falls: the Balcony Walk has no guardrails; swimming and jumps in Snake Gorge.
Cold nights on the rims; heat and dehydration on the plain; limited mobile coverage in wadis.
Strict law enforcement: alcohol, drugs, public behaviour, dress, Ramadan rules.
security.medicalAccess: Muscat has major hospitals; regional hospitals exist in Nizwa, Rustaq and Ibri but the mountain villages are 1–3 hours from them. Evacuation from Jebel Shams or Wadi Bani Awf may need helicopter or long road transfers; confirm insurance covers it.
security.insuranceConsiderations: Many insurers exclude destinations with government advice against travel or war risk. Canada, the US and Australia advise against or to reconsider travel, so cover for cancellation, medical evacuation and trekking or canyoning must be confirmed in writing before booking, including airspace closures.
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check France Diplomatie, FCDO, the Netherlands, Germany, Smartraveller and the US advisory before booking and two weeks before departure. Triggers to cancel or re-plan: any orange or red advice covering Ad Dakhiliyah, Ad Dhahirah or Al Batinah South; renewed strikes on Omani territory; closure of Muscat airspace; loss of insurance cover.

practicalRequirements.visa: Rules depend on the passport. France Diplomatie says French citizens receive a free entry stamp on arrival for stays up to 14 days (21 OMR for up to 30 days); the UK FCDO says British citizens can visit for up to 14 days without a visa. An eVisa (20 OMR for 30 days) can be requested up to a month ahead. Other nationalities must check.
practicalRequirements.entry: Border control may ask for a return ticket, proof of accommodation and proof of travel health insurance (FCDO).
practicalRequirements.passportValidity: At least six months beyond the date of exit from Oman (France Diplomatie, FCDO).
permits: No permit is needed for the planned route.
Photographing government and military sites is illegal; drones need a licence.
practicalRequirements.insurance: Travel insurance with adventure cover (canyoning, trekking up to about 2,000 m, 4x4 use), medical evacuation and cancellation from airspace closures; check the exclusions tied to advisories.
practicalRequirements.connectivity: Local SIM at Muscat airport; coverage is poor in wadis, on the Jebel Shams road and in the Wadi Bani Awf crossing. France recommends a satellite or GSM phone and a personal beacon in remote areas; check import and use rules for satellite devices before buying.
practicalRequirements.payments: Omani rial (OMR); cards are widely accepted in towns, cash needed at rim campsites, small guesthouses and fuel stops in the mountains.
practicalRequirements.medical: Standard vaccinations; yellow-fever certificate only when arriving from certain countries. Carry a prescription copy for medicines (some are banned).
practicalRequirements.fuel: Pump prices are fixed by the government: about 0.23–0.24 OMR per litre for M91/M95 in November 2026. Fill up before each mountain stage.

advantages: Genuinely different from the coastal-and-sands circuit: mountains, canyons, terrace villages and a UNESCO necropolis with few visitors.
Self-drive and camping suit the group's style; walking days are short and well defined.
Costs are moderate for four people in one vehicle, with a realistic total under the preferred ceiling.
Distances are short; no long driving days after the first day.
disadvantages: Security status is conditional: official advice conflicts and regional escalation could cancel flights or void insurance.
The 'other Oman' regions (Dhofar, Duqm, Musandam, the Empty Quarter) cannot be offered because of orange advice.
Cold nights on the rims, flash-flood risk and slow, narrow tracks.
The first day after an overnight flight is a 190 km drive that ends on a mountain track.
Fewer cultural 'immersions' than Southeast Asian or Andean routes; village stays are short.
uncertainties: Regional escalation, airspace closures and insurance exclusions given the conflicting advisories (Canada: avoid non-essential travel; US and Australia: reconsider travel, as summarised; UK: sudden escalation risk high).
Whether the rental company allows the Wadi Bani Awf track, Jebel Shams and the Jebel Akhdar road, covers off-road use and registers a second driver.
The 2027 Oman Air Paris–Muscat schedule and fares; no live quote was seen.
Exact Ramadan and Eid dates, and Eid-period crowding on 13–14 March.
Guide and operator availability and prices for Snake Gorge and Wadi Bani Habib.
Where to camp legally and safely on the Jebel Shams rim and at Balad Sayt; campsite fees were not found.
